messages:
maria: thinking out loud — instead of a monotonic percent-ramp for model upgrades, what if we do short 'pulse' exposures: tiny bursts to a broader cohort then back to baseline while we validate signals? keeps average risk low but surfaces regressions quickly :thinking_face:
kevin: can you sketch the API/config? console UX matters — pulses vs steps are different mental models
maria: rough sketch:

```
# pulses: series of exposures
pulses:
  - percent: 5
    duration_sec: 300   # 5m
    cooloff_sec: 1800   # 30m back to baseline
  - percent: 25
    duration_sec: 600
    cooloff_sec: 3600
```

```
# current simple ramp for comparison
ramp:
  - pct: 1
    duration_min: 30
  - pct: 5
    duration_min: 60
```
kevin: looks promising. main engineering concerns:
- telemetry tagging: need per-pulse aggregation windows + an easy marker to indicate which requests were in-pulse
- quotas & burst capacity: pulses can create transient concurrency spikes; need burst-guards on dedicated pools
joyce: +1 on tagging. add a pulse_id header so traces/logs can be filtered. also make sure prefix-caching isn't permanently warmed by pulse traffic
nana: from console POV, pulses should render as tiny sparklines on a timeline and support hover-to-expand. transient regressions are easy to miss without that visual cue
maria: proposal: add header "x-redwood-pulse-id" and a trace tag "pulse_exposed". Observability can do pulse-aware rollups
observability-bot: FYI: detailed per-route metrics retention is 14d. pulse-analysis might need extended retention or on-the-fly rollups to avoid losing short-lived signals :bell:
kevin: rollout guards: if error_rate > 0.5% during pulse window OR latency_p99 > 30% vs baseline -> auto-fallback. these rules must be pluggable per-customer
maria: edge-case: tiny pulses = noisy stats. add min_samples param (e.g., 100) so guards only evaluate when sample size is adequate
joyce: API example updated:

```
pulses:
  - id: smoke-1
    percent: 3
    duration_sec: 300
    cooloff_sec: 1800
    min_samples: 200
    fallbacks:
      - condition: err_rate > 0.005
        action: rollback
```
kevin: UX Q: how do we scope pulses by geography/region? we should allow region-scoped pulses so EU customers can be isolated from US bursts
maria: add optional region and pool tags. also include observation_window param to control whether we align aggregation to pulse duration or use a fixed window for more stable comparison
ana: console should also show a simulated 24h steady-state exposure (average exposure if pulses run continuously). PMs need that to estimate cost and steady-state risk
joyce: implementation note: route-level cache TTLs must honor pulse flags to avoid cache poisoning. suggest short TTL overrides for pulse keys and explicit cache-key segregation
maria: next steps:
- eng-platform: finalize API shape (kevin + maria)
- observability: add pulse_id tag, define retention and rollups (joyce + observability)
- console: timeline view + simulation card (ana)
I'll draft a short RFC and tracking ticket. :rocket:
deploy-bot: New RFC created: rfc/2261 - "Pulse-based canary exposures" — https://redwood/ops/rfc/2261
ana: added mockups to the RFC page
kevin: let's sync Thu 11am to lock the shape. :calendar?
